title: Strategy Anchorboard and Initiative Routing Protocol
creator: Priya Shah
description: Create a lightweight, operational playbook (the 'Strategy Anchorboard') and an associated Initiative Routing Protocol to reduce cross-team OKR conflicts and accelerate decision handoffs. The Anchorboard is a single-pane representation that maps company-level OKRs to initiative anchors, shows ownership lanes, conflict scores, and routing rules for when initiatives overlap. This ticket covers the PM-side spec, stakeholder reviews, and a pilot with infra, console, and research teams.
goals: Reduce ambiguous ownership for company-level initiatives by 80% during planning windows
Establish a routable escalation path that cuts cross-team decision latency to <72 hours for priority initiatives
Surface high-risk initiative overlaps to execs automatically during weekly roadmap syncs
acceptance_criteria: Anchorboard prototype populated for current quarter OKRs with accurate ownership and conflict scores
Routing protocol documented (steps, roles, SLAs) and validated with three partner teams
Pilot feedback collected and >70% of pilot participants rate the routing flow as an improvement to prior process
Playbook published to Confluence and linked in product planning templates
deliverables: Initiative Routing Protocol doc with decision provenance template
Pilot dataset: 12 active initiatives mapped and conflict-scored
One walkthrough session and one async feedback run with stakeholders
stakeholders: Luca Moreno - Director, Serving Runtime (pilot partner)
Sara Liu - Head of Design (UI for anchorboard)
Miguel Alvarez - Head of Research (evaluation metrics)

decisions: Adopt a conflict scoring heuristic based on overlap of ownership, shared dependencies, and release windows (weights: ownership=0.5, dependencies=0.3, release-overlap=0.2)
Routing protocol will use a three-tier escalation (owner -> track lead -> program PM) with 48/72 hour SLAs depending on priority
Anchorboard UI will be a minimal read/write table embedded in Confluence first; later move to Console if pilot succeeds
risks: Teams may not keep ownership fields up to date — mitigated by adding a weekly ownership reminder to the sync agenda
Conflict scores could produce noise if thresholds are too low — mitigation: threshold tuning during pilot and manual review for high-sensitivity cases
Engineering bandwidth for automation (freshness jobs) is limited — fallback to manual refresh cadence for Q2
notes: Trade-off: start with Confluence embed vs building Console dashboard. Chosen to prioritize speed of adoption and lower engineering lift.
Measure success via: reduction in routing cycle time, % of initiatives with single owner, and qualitative pilot feedback.
Next step: finalize conflict scoring data schema with infra (ENG-1842) and produce a 1-hour demo for exec roadmap sync on 2026-03-18.
